author: pelican state news
title: New Orleans committee reviews city budget and financial measures for 2026
text:
The Budget, Audit, and Board of Review Committee in New Orleans met on May 19 to discuss the city’s financial status for the first quarter of 2026 and review several budget-related ordinances.
The meeting focused on efforts by both the Moreno Administration and the New Orleans City Council to address a significant budget crisis inherited at the start of the year. The committee heard a presentation from Chief Administrative Officer Joe Giarrusso about recent steps taken to stabilize finances, including identifying new revenue sources such as funds from the Caesars lease agreement, Municipal and Traffic Court, and the Assessor’s Office. The city has also maintained its $36 million savings fund while securing a $125 million Revenue Anticipation Note to support payroll operations. Additionally, officials reduced spending by $73 million compared to last year’s budget.
Cost-containment measures have played a key role in these efforts. According to Giarrusso’s report, overtime spending was cut by nearly half, a hiring freeze was instituted, positions were consolidated, travel costs were reduced, and operations were streamlined. A targeted furlough program generated approximately $1.13 million in savings.
Despite these initiatives, Giarrusso said that “one-time revenues alone will not resolve the City’s structural challenges.” He said that more recurring revenue measures and operational efficiencies would be proposed later this year as part of an ongoing effort toward long-term fiscal sustainability.
The committee also voted on several pieces of legislation related to the city budget during this session. Meeting materials—including agendas and presentations—are available online for public review.
City officials indicated that continued disciplined cash management will be necessary moving forward as they work toward restoring stable finances for New Orleans.
